title: Norway Spruce: Old Norway Spruces You Can Visit
meta_description: The spruce of Europe's mountain forests. Old Tjikko in Sweden is a five-metre tree on a root system carbon-dated to about 9,550 years.
intro: Norway spruce belongs to the mountain forests of Scandinavia and central Europe, and on a Swedish fell it may hold the oldest living thing on this site. Old Tjikko, on Fulufjället, is a scrappy spruce about five metres tall whose visible trunk is only a few centuries old; the root system beneath it has been carbon-dated to about 9,550 years, sending up a new trunk each time the last one dies. Lithuania's Witch's Spruce breaks at knee height into eighteen stems that climb together to 32 metres, a habit specialists know of nowhere else in Europe. In cities it is always somebody's choice. Sofia's tallest was planted in 1885 by the writer Ivan Vazov and has outgrown the bust raised to him later, and Helsinki's Independence Spruce was sown on 6 December 1917, the day the Finnish Parliament accepted the declaration of independence.
